findings.summary: The executable lifecycle oracle can reach `deleted-tombstoned` without proving the ratified policy's authoritative trigger-event or qualified-human disposition contract. The policy requires duplicate-key-rejecting eventVersion 2 events with exact organization, item/environment, record class and revision, actor and authority, policy, correlation, occurred time and durable timestamp authority, provider record, and event-specific members. The bound LIFECYCLE-EVENT schema instead accepts a separate simplified v1 derived event; its signed trigger history has no schema, and deriveLifecycleBoundary trusts rows containing only type, at, and recordId. An independently resealed history row with eventVersion `999`, organization `attacker-tenant`, and timestampAuthority `browser-caller` still produced `deleted-tombstoned` with lifecycle effect 1. The same accepted raw-erasure path uses RAW-POLICY-GRANT v2 records that omit the policy-mandated sanitizer/inspector revisions, allowed temporary-copy providers, safeguards, terminal event, 60-second deadline, erase method, source-original exclusion, complete-inventory rule, signer identity/current qualification, session, authorization policy, and provider proof; an ordinary fixture-local signature plus signerRole string suffices. Thus malformed, wrong-tenant, caller-timed, or under-authorized inputs can satisfy the oracle before deletion or cryptographic erasure.
findings.requiredResolution: Replace the simplified lifecycle trigger with a closed schema and semantic path for every exact policy event and event-specific member. Verify each event's stable actor, current authority, provider record/proof, organization/item/class/revision/policy/correlation, server or provider time, ordering, signature, and duplicate-free bytes before deriving expiry. Define one provider-bound qualified-human disposition/raw-grant envelope carrying the complete A10.1 identity, hat, qualification, session, policy, target, inventory, hold/reference, safeguards, allowed-copy/provider, source-original exclusion, deadline, erase method, and conditions. Test wrong/missing/extra/duplicate/stale/wrong-tenant/caller-time events and absent, unqualified, transferred, revoked, wrong-hat, wrong-session, wrong-copy/provider, source-original, safeguard-missing, provider-proof-missing, replay, and race authorities with typed zero effects. Refresh every affected digest, obtain a new exact qualified-human ruling, and repeat exact-revision review.

findings.summary: The incorporated migration definition is not backed by the exhaustive executable matrix promised by R4 and required to close the original blocker. The control fixture has no migration execution collection or migration journal/plan/cleanup schema. Its ten migration rows exercise only the generic protected-action authorization decision; even the positive expand row reports providerRequest 1 but migration effect 0. The validator has no migration execution loop and never proves expand/backfill/contract state or pre/post canonical truth. The permissions actions also carry only plan, journal, tenant-inventory, backup, and rollback-consequence digests: no closed cleanup-authorization record or migration-plan schema makes the human decision name and validate the exact columns/data, batch/checkpoint, supported old/new readers and writers, application rollback state, affected tenants, or provider result. Therefore all declared IDs can pass without executing interruption at every checkpoint, mixed-version compatibility, app rollback, two-runner/idempotent recovery, exact destructive scope, data/signature/audit preservation, or one journaled result/safe non-result.
findings.requiredResolution: Add closed schemas for the signed migration plan, cleanup authorization, journal/checkpoint, provider result, backup/PITR, restoration, and pre/post truth inventory. Bind exact columns/data and affected tenants rather than opaque unvalidated digests. Execute every supported schema/app version across expand, every backfill batch/checkpoint, contract, concurrent old/new reads and writes, application rollback before/during/after backfill, interruption before/after each effect, retry/replay, two-runner race, stale/wrong-tenant/wrong-column cleanup, partial/unknown provider result, recovery, and restore. Compare exact item, signature, attempt, audit, release, evidence, and data truth; prove one journaled result or safe non-result and typed zero effects for every denial; require declared-versus-executed set equality at the final Exam revision.
